title: Bring-Your-Model Beta — internal announce crib
content:
Notes + talking points for a quick internal announcement and Q&A thread about the Bring-Your-Own-Model (BYOM) beta. This is a personal scratchpad — messy, prioritized for speed.

Goal:
- Announce limited BYOM beta to product/dev teams and early partners.
- Set expectations: early, opt-in, limited capacity, security review required.
- Give predictable support routing and SLOs for participants.

Audience:
- Internal engineers + ML Eng + Solutions + Sales AE leads + Customer Success managers for participating accounts.
- ~50 people across eng/product/GTM.

Topline message (one-liner for Slack/email header):
- "Internal: BYOM beta is live — opt-in program for partners to serve their models through Redwood’s serving runtime (limited seats). Read quick details + FAQs."

Channels & cadence:
- Quick Slack announcement in #eng #product #gts (short blurb + link to signup doc).
- Follow-up email to AE/CS leads with onboarding checklist.
- Office hours Drop-in (30m) 48 hours after announce — hosted by Marcus + Asha.

Who handles what:
- Marcus: announce + host initial drop-in + triage incoming ask.
- Asha: security/KMS checklist and readiness signoff for accounts.
- Rae: infra capacity gating and autoscaler guardrails.
- Leo: sample config + quickstart repo link + support playbook.

Draft Slack blurb (short):
- "Heads-up: BYOM beta is open for signups. This lets select partners run their own model artifacts through Redwood’s inference runtime (we provide secure routing, monitoring, and optional KV prefix caching). Seats limited. Sign up here: <signup doc link>. For technical onboarding join office hours on Thu 10:00 PST."

Longer internal note (for AE/CS):
- What it is: managed path for customers to bring their model weights. We run inference on behalf of the customer in a VPC-isolated runtime. Customers keep model ownership; Redwood provides serving, telemetry, and optional optimization.
- Limitations for beta: max 4 concurrent models per customer, quantization/format must be ONNX or SFT-quantized PyTorch (docs linked), no autop-run deployments (manual deploys only).
- Security: must complete KMS onboarding + model handling attestation. No public model hosting in this beta.
- Support: 72-hour response target for P1 issues, SRE escalation via #sre-oncall. No SLA for latency during beta.

Key talking points for drop-in / manager prep:
- Why BYOM: customers want to keep IP & fine-tuned weights while offloading infra. This opens revenue motion for Dedicated/Private customers and helps tighten our product roadmap for model-variant routing.
- What it means for teams: more model variants to manage in runtime; expect short-term increased telemetry noise. Product/Optimize will recommend batch/cache settings per workload.
- Risk posture: early, experimental — security-first gate for access. SRE/infra will throttle new pods to protect shared capacity.

Anticipated questions + suggested answers (crib):
- Q: "Can customers bring any model?"
  A: Not yet — beta supports ONNX + quantized PyTorch. We’ll expand formats after we validate stability and security.
- Q: "Will Redwood fine-tune or host models long-term?"
  A: Customers retain model ownership; Redwood operates the serving runtime. We offer optional managed quantization/optimization.
- Q: "Is customer data inspected or used to improve our models?"
  A: No. Data flow is strictly from customer request -> runtime -> response. Telemetry for infra/perf is collected, but no training data is harvested.
- Q: "How do we price this?"
  A: Beta pricing is opt-in flat monthly + usage buffer; finance/ops is drafting a recommended pilot pricing sheet. For now route pricing questions to Brian (go-to-market finance).
- Q: "What happens if model causes high latency or spins up lots of GPU?"
  A: We’ll enforce per-account resource caps and autoscale limits. Infra has tools to throttle and failover to a Redwood-verified compatible model if the customer opts in to fallback.

Immediate open issues to resolve (for the announce to link to):
- (BYOM-1422) final signup form + intake validation (ownership + KMS proof). Pending: form link. Owner: Marcus.
- (BYOM-1427) sample ONNX conversion guide — small edge cases. Owner: Leo.
- Security attestation template for partner legal. Owner: Asha.

Prep checklist for signups (short):
- Customer completes intake form + KMS key material (or HSM reference).
- Security review signed by Asha.
- Infra capacity check + account quota set by Rae.
- Support playbook assigned (assign CS lead + contact info).

Office hours plan (30 min):
- 0-5m: Quick status + what BYOM enables (Marcus).
- 5-15m: Security checklist walk-thru (Asha).
- 15-25m: How to onboard (Leo) — sample repo + deploy steps.
- 25-30m: Open Q&A and note-taker capture to Google Drive.

Follow-ups post-announcement:
- Publish short "how to route questions" doc in #gcs and add to internal BYOM confluence.
- Triage list of interested customers; convert to intake tickets and tag with BYOM-beta.
- Weekly sync with SRE + Product to review telemetry for beta cohort.

Tone notes for comms:
- Emphasize opt-in, secure, limited seats. Avoid overpromising performance. Put a clear beta disclaimer.
- Use approachable language; include technical links for engineers but keep header plain-English for GTM folks.

Slack quick links to include in final announce (placeholders):
- Signup form: <TODO: intake form link>
- Office hours calendar: <TODO: calendar link>
- BYOM quickstart repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/byom-quickstart

Tasks before publish (this week):
- Finalize intake form (Marcus, today)
- Draft short email to AE/CS with onboarding checklist (Marcus + Leo, tomorrow)
- Publish beta announcement in #eng (Marcus, Thu)

Random scratch notes / TODO / ideas:
- Consider an explicit "fallback policy" checkbox on intake: allow Redwood to auto-fallback to verified models in outage. Helps protect infra.
- Small badge for participating accounts in Console to show BYOM-enabled status. UX idea for product.
- Quick internal metric dashboard: BYOM requests per minute, avg latency, top model types. Rae to wire up a dashboard fragment.

End of scratchpad. Save this as working draft; will prune into short announce + FAQ doc once intake link and security attestation are ready.

-- Marcus
